evidence.title: APC seeks moratorium extension into 2027
evidence.supports: Confirms the initial (original) moratorium term was two months, and that the Area Plan Commission recommended -- and commissioners later adopted -- a 12-month extension running to Feb. 24, 2027. The original 2-month term (~60 days) is what duration_days should reflect, and it already does.
evidence.quote: President Robert Braun believed that the (2-month) initial timeframe wasn't nearly long enough and felt an extension was needed. ... the APC chose to give a favorable recommendation to commissioners for a 12-month extension of the data center moratorium that is currently in place until Feb. 24, 2026.

evidence.title: Franklin Co. Commissioners Place Year-Long Moratorium on Data Centers
evidence.supports: Confirms commissioners voted unanimously to extend the moratorium through Feb. 24, 2027, matching the row's current_end_date_iso.
evidence.quote: Franklin County Commissioners have voted unanimously to keep a year-long data center moratorium in place. The moratorium will prevent applications for building a data center until February 24, 2027.

decisions.notes: DURATION_MISMATCH resolved as no change: the duration text's first number (12 months) is the EXTENSION, not the original term; the original moratorium (in place until Feb. 24, 2026, i.e., from about Dec. 24, 2025) was two months, so duration_days=60 already correctly reflects the original term.

evidence.title: Grant County adopts 24-month moratorium on data-center permits
evidence.supports: Ordinance 4-2026's operative scope, as adopted March 16, 2026, covers only improvement-location permits and applications for structures connected to data centers; no mention of cryptocurrency mining.
evidence.quote: The ordinance, approved unanimously, halts issuance or receipt of improvement-location permits and related applications for structures connected to data centers until the Area Planning Commission completes a study and recommends amendments to the county zoning ordinance.

evidence.title: Grant County subcommittee advances data center ordinance draft, debates crypto inclusion, power and noise limits
evidence.supports: Confirms cryptocurrency mining is only under discussion for the future PERMANENT zoning ordinance the subcommittee is drafting -- not part of the already-adopted temporary moratorium (Ordinance 4-2026) this row tracks; no binding decision to include crypto had been made.
evidence.quote: The advisory subcommittee discussed whether cryptocurrency mining should be regulated in the same ordinance as data centers or in a separate rule. ... The group agreed to leave language in the draft for now and revisit the issue later when more information is available. ... No formal, binding votes occurred; the subcommittee's edits are advisory.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved as no change: cryptocurrency mining is only being debated for a future permanent ordinance, not covered by the currently-effective moratorium (Ordinance 4-2026). sectors stays ["data_center"].

current_end_date_iso.reason: News coverage describes the Aug. 4, 2026 action as extending the moratorium 'from six months to a full year' -- i.e., the total term becomes twelve months from the original June 2026 adoption, not twelve months measured from the August extension vote. 2026-06-16 (the row's date_enacted_iso) + 12 months = 2027-06-16.

evidence.title: Madison County commissioners extend data center moratorium for full year
evidence.supports: Confirms the Aug. 4, 2026 commissioners' vote extended the (originally six-month) data-center moratorium to a full year, following the Planning Commission's recommendation to do so.
evidence.quote: Commissioners in Madison County have voted to extend a moratorium on data center projects for a full year.

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE resolved with an approximate/interpreted date (2027-06-16); no source states the exact new end date numerically, but the reporting is consistent in describing this as converting the original six-month term into a full year from original adoption, matching the row's own current_status.

sectors.reason: News coverage of the Nov. 17, 2025 vote and the legal_basis text both confirm the moratorium's operative scope explicitly includes wind energy systems, not just solar and data centers.

evidence.title: 3 counties put moratoriums on data center projects
evidence.supports: Confirms Putnam County's moratorium, as passed, explicitly covers wind energy systems alongside solar and data centers.
evidence.quote: On Tuesday, Putnam County did just that, passing a one-year moratorium on wind, solar, data centers and small modular nuclear reactor projects.

evidence.title: Putnam County Commissioners vote in favor of moratorium on solar farms
evidence.supports: Confirms the moratorium as voted 2-1 by commissioners covers solar farms, data centers, and wind energy systems, running until Nov. 17, 2026.
evidence.quote: urging commissioners to vote in favor of a one year moratorium on solar farms, as well as data centers, wind energy systems, solar energy conservation systems. ... the commissioners voted 2-1 in favor of the moratorium, which will be in place until Nov. 17, 2026.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved: wind is expressly part of the moratorium's operative scope (matching the ordinance title already in legal_basis, 'small modular reactors, data centers, solar energy conservation systems, and wind energy systems'), so sectors gains "wind". Small modular reactors are not added since 'general'/nuclear is not a listed sector category and is out of scope for this flag.
